OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The card's own `if not target.is_gone:` is DELETED and PowerCmd.apply now carries the WHOLE of `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-322): `cmds.can_receive_powers` is `not target.is_removed_from_combat and hooks.should_allow_hitting(target)`, and `Creature.is_removed_from_combat` (creatures.py) is `is_gone and not retained_after_death` -- the sim's expression of `CombatState == null`, since it never drops a corpse from `enemies` (conformance addresses enemies by index). The two edits are a MATCHED PAIR: round 6 had wired only the ShouldAllowHitting half here, so deleting the card guard on its own would have powered the ordinary corpse that CreatureCmd.cs:523-531 removes. Pinned by test/test_can_receive_powers.py -- ordinary corpse refused, removal-vetoed corpse powered, mid-revival corpse still refused. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE: the observable the entry proposed -- a Vicious draw off a retained corpse -- is not reachable in the sim's SHIPPED content, and the enumeration is the finding. Every sim producer of a retained corpse also makes it unhittable for as long as it lasts (IllusionPower.cs:95-105, AdaptablePower.cs:68-78 and ReattachPower.cs:74-86 each pair the removal veto with ShouldAllowHitting), the sole exception being a Decimillipede segment killed with every other segment already down -- and that ends the combat, so PowerCmd.Apply's own IsEnding guard (PowerCmd.cs:69-72) swallows it first. The game's third case, PainfulStabsPower.cs:29-32 on Test Subject phase 2, retains WITHOUT vetoing hits and the sim's PainfulStabsPower omits that override; recorded here rather than fixed, because it is not this entry's line. The code is now the source's shape either way.  The text it replaced read: The damage, the ordering and every amount are faithful; the divergence is the sim's extra `if not target.is_gone:` guard before the debuff. C# applies it unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that dead creatures CAN still receive powers -- it refuses only when `CombatState == null` (the corpse was REMOVED) or ShouldAllowHitting says no. The two agree for an ordinary monster, because `CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `await Kill(...)` before returning (CreatureCmd.cs:409) and `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition` removes the creature at CreatureCmd.cs:523-525. They diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; modelled in the sim as `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104, for ReattachPower/Decimillipede), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower, which draws on any Vulnerable the owner applies with no liveness test on the target (ViciousPower.cs:19-26; sim port powers.py:1160-1179): hold Vicious, kill a retained-corpse enemy with this card -- the game draws, the sim does not. LIVE; card/vicious, ViciousPower and the retained-corpse path are all ported. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3). EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/card_probes.py dead-target-guards` lists 41 sim card classes that test liveness.
